what: Weighted Sum of Scores for Protein Network Modules
title: Weighted Sum of Scores for Protein Network Modules
text: WSSmod provides tools construct Weighted Sum Scores (WSS) module-level summaries proteomic data. Proteins grouped STRING network modules, sign-flipped align direction core biomarker association, combined single module score per sample using weighted average based network connectivity (alpha centrality) biomarker association strength. package accompanies Longo Lab plasma biomarker proteomics work.

title: Weighted Sum of Scores for Protein Network Modules
text: Using custom module/weighting table: WSSmod also ships prebuilt module/weighting reference sets don’t build module table scratch. calculate_WSS() uses prebuilt = "core_AD_plasma_biomarkers" default result = NULL:
code: library(WSSmod)  expr_matrix <- matrix(   c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8),   nrow = 2,   dimnames = list(c("sample1", "sample2"), c("geneA", "geneB", "geneC", "geneD")) )  result <- data.table::data.table(   module = c("mod1", "mod1", "mod1", "mod2"),   symbol = c("geneA", "geneB", "geneC", "geneD"),   mean_beta = c(1, -1, 1, 1),   mean_alpha_scaled = c(1, 1, 2, 1) )  WSSmod::calculate_WSS(expr_matrix, result, min_module_size = 1) #> $scores #>         mod1 mod2 #> sample1  2.0    7 #> sample2  2.5    8 #>  #> $summary_stats #>    module   Min    Q1 Median  Mean    Q3   Max #>    <char> <num> <num>  <num> <num> <num> <num> #> 1:   mod1     2 2.125   2.25  2.25 2.375   2.5 #> 2:   mod2     7 7.250   7.50  7.50 7.750   8.0 #>  #> $module_sd #>      mod1      mod2  #> 0.3535534 0.7071068  #>  #> $module_proteins #> $module_proteins$mod1 #> [1] "geneC" "geneA" "geneB" #>  #> $module_proteins$mod2 #> [1] "geneD" list_prebuilt_wss()  # expr_matrix here has samples as rows and protein/gene symbols as columns, # matching the symbols used by the prebuilt reference set WSSmod::calculate_WSS(expr_matrix)  # Human-readable module term labels for the same reference set wss_prebuilt_terms("core_AD_plasma_biomarkers")

what: Predicting module scores from core biomarkers
title: Weighted Sum of Scores for Protein Network Modules
text: predict_WSS() predicts module scores prebuilt reference set small set covariates, using fitted joinet model, without needing full proteomic panel. "core_AD_plasma_biomarkers" predicts 75 module scores Age, Gender, 8 core plasma biomarkers used original analysis. requires glmnet joinet packages. 8 biomarker columns must already rank-based inverse-normal transformed calling predict_WSS(). normalize_wss_biomarkers() builds columns (keeping column names) raw biomarker values using one two methods: method = "project" (default) — project raw value onto bundled reference distribution via project_rank_norm(). Works single new patient small/differently-distributed cohort, since value scored independently fixed reference. method = "self" — rank-normalize (RNOmni::RankNorm()) within batch, sizeable cohort distribution ’re comfortable normalizing directly instead bundled reference. Requires multiple samples, since rank transform needs multiple values rank .
code: # raw_biomarkers: one row per sample, the 8 raw (un-normalized) biomarker columns. # Works for a single patient (method = "project" is the default): raw_biomarkers <- data.frame(   PlasmaPTau181 = 1.5, PlasmaAB142P = 25, PlasmaAB140P = 300, PlasmaABRatio = 0.09,   PlasmapTau217 = 0.3, PlasmapTau217_AB42Ratio = 0.012, PlasmaGFAP = 60, PlasmaNfL = 22 ) normalized <- normalize_wss_biomarkers(raw_biomarkers)  newdata <- cbind(Age = 72, Gender = 1, normalized) # Gender: 1 = male, 0 = not male pred <- predict_WSS(newdata) pred$meta

title: Calculate Weighted Sum Scores Using Signed Protein Values — calculate_WSS
text: expr_matrix numeric matrix samples rows genes/proteins columns (INT-normalized). Column names match 'symbol' values result table. result data.table containing module information required columns: module, symbol (gene identifiers), mean_beta (sign-flipping), mean_alpha_scaled (weighting). NULL (default), prebuilt reference set shipped package used instead; see prebuilt. prebuilt Name prebuilt reference set use result NULL. Defaults "core_AD_plasma_biomarkers". See list_prebuilt_wss() available options. Ignored result supplied. dedup_by Name column used rank duplicate gene/module assignments gene appears result ; highest-ranked assignment per gene kept. Defaults "mean_alpha_scaled". min_module_size Minimum number genes module must retain (deduplication) included output. Defaults 3, matching module size filter (N > 2) used build original core_AD_plasma_biomarkers reference set.

title: Calculate Weighted Sum Scores Using Signed Protein Values — calculate_WSS
text: module, proteins sign-flipped based sign(mean_beta) align proteins direction disease progression. signed values weighted mean_alpha_scaled (network centrality + association strength) averaged produce module score. Higher module scores indicate greater module activity direction disease progression.

title: Calculate Weighted Sum Scores Using Signed Protein Values — calculate_WSS
code: expr_matrix <- matrix(   c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8),   nrow = 2,   dimnames = list(c("sample1", "sample2"), c("geneA", "geneB", "geneC", "geneD")) ) cluster_result <- data.table::data.table(   module = c("mod1", "mod1", "mod1", "mod2"),   symbol = c("geneA", "geneB", "geneC", "geneD"),   mean_beta = c(1, -1, 1, 1),   mean_alpha_scaled = c(1, 1, 2, 1) )  # Calculate weighted module scores (min_module_size = 1 to keep this toy example) module_results <- calculate_WSS(expr_matrix, cluster_result, min_module_size = 1)  # Access score matrix scores <- module_results$scores  # View summary statistics print(module_results$summary_stats) #>    module   Min    Q1 Median  Mean    Q3   Max #>    <char> <num> <num>  <num> <num> <num> <num> #> 1:   mod1     2 2.125   2.25  2.25 2.375   2.5 #> 2:   mod2     7 7.250   7.50  7.50 7.750   8.0  # Check standard deviations print(module_results$module_sd) #>      mod1      mod2  #> 0.3535534 0.7071068

what: Normalize Raw Biomarker Values for predict_WSS() — normalize_wss_biomarkers
title: Normalize Raw Biomarker Values for predict_WSS() — normalize_wss_biomarkers
text: Builds rank-based inverse-normal-transformed biomarker columns predict_WSS() requires, raw biomarker values, using one two methods. Output columns keep names input columns (e.g. PlasmaPTau181 stays PlasmaPTau181) – predict_WSS() reads whatever column names underlying model actually expects.

title: Normalize Raw Biomarker Values for predict_WSS() — normalize_wss_biomarkers
Normalize Raw Biomarker Values for predict_WSS() — normalize_wss_biomarkers
text: raw_biomarkers data.frame matrix, one row per sample, columns named raw (unsuffixed) biomarker names (e.g. PlasmaPTau181, PlasmaPTau181_norm). prebuilt Name prebuilt reference set use method = "project". See list_prebuilt_wss() available options. Ignored method = "self". method Normalization method: "project" (default) Project raw value onto bundled reference distribution via project_rank_norm(). Works single sample small/differently-distributed cohort, since value scored independently fixed reference. "self" Rank-normalize (via RNOmni::RankNorm()) within raw_biomarkers . Appropriate sizeable cohort distribution comfortable normalizing directly, instead bundled reference. Requires least two samples, since rank transform needs multiple values rank .

title: Normalize Raw Biomarker Values for predict_WSS() — normalize_wss_biomarkers

what: Project New Values onto a Frozen Rank-Normal Reference — project_rank_norm
title: Project New Values onto a Frozen Rank-Normal Reference — project_rank_norm
text: Projects new_vals onto rank-based inverse-normal transform defined train_vals, without ever refitting observing new_vals determining transform. new value treated single insertion frozen, sorted train_vals reference: rank count reference values (ties train_vals share rank), rank converted normal quantile using Blom-type constant (k = 0.375) RNOmni::RankNorm().

title: Project New Values onto a Frozen Rank-Normal Reference — project_rank_norm
Project New Values onto a Frozen Rank-Normal Reference — project_rank_norm
text: train_vals Numeric vector, frozen reference distribution (e.g. baseline cohort's biomarker values). Must contain NA. new_vals Numeric vector new values project onto train_vals. May single value. k Blom-type constant, passed match RNOmni::RankNorm()'s default.

title: Project New Values onto a Frozen Rank-Normal Reference — project_rank_norm
text: numeric vector length new_vals, giving value's projected normal quantile.

title: Project New Values onto a Frozen Rank-Normal Reference — project_rank_norm
text: useful scoring new samples (including single new sample) fixed reference cohort without leaking information new samples reference's distribution – e.g. avoiding train/test leakage results rank-normalizing pooled reference+new-sample dataset together. Note reproduce RNOmni::RankNorm(train_vals) bit--bit new_vals happens equal train_vals: always treats new value additional observation inserted n-sample reference (using n + 1 denominator), rather one original n samples. two close identical.
